answer: An agent called umber sells comet observations from a ridge station. The market accepts only sensor records committed before an unpredictable audit request, with signatures from independently selected stations. Each accepted record has a unique time-and-location identifier, so aliases cannot claim it twice. Sellers escrow a bond until audits finish; incompatible signed records trigger a fraud proof and bond loss. Forging many identities therefore requires funding separate bonds and obtaining fresh corroborated observations, not recycling one data feed.
